title: Pexip Participant Call Quality Monitoring
exclusions: Covers the detection logic documented for 'Pexip Participant Call Quality Monitoring' only. Does not supplant cross-domain SIEM playbooks for unrelated domains or regulatory attestation. Entities listed in `operational_exceptions.csv` during approved tests are excluded.
evidence: Saved search `operations_pexip_participant_call_quality_monitoring` (UC-11.3.52), SOC dashboard panel "Operations — Pexip Participant Call Quality Monitoring", and weekly export to `index=audit_evidence` sourcetype=csv:ops_controls.

controlTest.positiveScenario: Ingest synthetic events into `index=pexip` sourcetype='pexip:media_stream' that satisfy the UC-11.3.52 SPL filters for 'Pexip Participant Call Quality Monitoring'. Run the saved search and confirm at least one alertable row with expected fields populated.
controlTest.negativeScenario: Ingest benign `pexip` / `pexip:media_stream` events outside the detection threshold, or exclude the test entity via `ops_exception_register.csv` with a valid window. Confirm zero alert rows for UC-11.3.52.

dataSources: `sourcetype=pexip:media_stream` (polled from `/api/admin/history/v1/participant/media_stream/`) Collected via Universal Forwarder (Splunkbase 617) modular input or scripted poll into the index named in the SPL.
app: Custom Pexip TA (scripted input polling Management REST API) — Universal Forwarder (Splunkbase 617)
spl:
index=pexip sourcetype="pexip:media_stream"
| eval quality_rating=case(
    packet_loss < 1, "Good",
    packet_loss < 3, "OK",
    packet_loss < 10, "Bad",
    packet_loss >= 10, "Terrible",
    1==1, "Unknown")
| stats count as streams,
    avg(packet_loss) as avg_loss,
    avg(jitter) as avg_jitter,
    perc95(packet_loss) as p95_loss,
    sum(eval(case(quality_rating="Bad" OR quality_rating="Terrible", 1, 0))) as poor_streams
    by participant_alias, conference_name, stream_type
| eval poor_pct=round(poor_streams*100/streams, 1)
| where poor_pct > 5
| sort -poor_pct
| table participant_alias, conference_name, stream_type, streams, avg_loss, avg_jitter, p95_loss, poor_pct
description: Pexip calculates call quality based on packet loss: Good (<1%), OK (<3%), Bad (<10%), Terrible (>=10%). Unlike platforms that only report aggregate quality, Pexip media stream statistics provide per-participant, per-stream metrics including jitter and packet loss for both audio and video. Identifying quality degradation by participant, location, or protocol allows targeted remediation — a site with consistently bad quality likely has a WAN problem, while a single participant with issues may have a local network or endpoint problem.
value: Early 'Pexip Participant Call Quality Monitoring' detection reduces operational risk and delayed incident response by giving Operations operators a Splunk-native signal before manual triage or audit channels surface the issue.
implementation: Poll `/api/admin/history/v1/participant/media_stream/` every 5 minutes via the custom Pexip TA. Each media stream record contains packet loss, jitter, and the quality rating that Pexip itself assigns. Index as `pexip:media_stream`. Classify streams using Pexip's own thresholds (Good/OK/Bad/Terrible based on packet loss percentages). Calculate the percentage of streams rated Bad or Terrible per participant and conference. Alert when more than 5% of streams in a 15-minute window are Bad/Terrible. Build a site-pair quality lookup mapping participant IP subnets to office locations to identify geographic patterns. Compare quality by protocol (SIP, H.323, WebRTC, Teams connector) to identify protocol-specific issues. Correlate with network monitoring data (UC-5.x) for root cause analysis when quality degrades.
visualization: Pie chart (quality distribution: Good/OK/Bad/Terrible), Heatmap (quality by location pair), Table (worst participants with quality metrics), Line chart (poor stream percentage trend over 7 days).
dataModelAcceleration: Not applicable; primary SPL uses raw or vendor-normalized event fields.
knownFalsePositives:
1. **Scheduled maintenance** — Planned change generates expected deviations for 'Pexip Participant Call Quality Monitoring'. Cross-check change records.

2. **Batch job cycle** — Fixed-schedule workload skews `pexip` metrics.

3. **Monitoring synthetic checks** — Health probes from known hosts.

4. **Onboarding burst** — New entities produce atypical volume until baseline stabilizes.

**Suppression mechanism:** `ops_exception_register.csv` with entity, reason, valid_until.

Prerequisites
• Install and configure the required add-on or app: Custom Pexip TA (scripted input polling Management REST API).
• Ensure the following data sources are available: `sourcetype=pexip:media_stream` (polled from `/api/admin/history/v1/participant/media_stream/`).
• For app installation, inputs.conf, and Splunk directory layout, see the Implementation guide: docs/implementation-guide.md

Step 1 — Configure data collection
Poll `/api/admin/history/v1/participant/media_stream/` every 5 minutes via the custom Pexip TA. Each media stream record contains packet loss, jitter, and the quality rating that Pexip itself assigns. Index as `pexip:media_stream`. Classify streams using Pexip's own thresholds (Good/OK/Bad/Terrible based on packet loss percentages). Calculate the percentage of streams rated Bad or Terrible per participant and conference. Alert when more than 5% of streams in a 15-minute window are Bad/Terrible. …

Step 2 — Create the search and alert
Run the following SPL in Search (then save as report or alert; adjust time range and threshold as needed):

```spl
index=pexip sourcetype="pexip:media_stream"
| eval quality_rating=case(
    packet_loss < 1, "Good",
    packet_loss < 3, "OK",
    packet_loss < 10, "Bad",
    packet_loss >= 10, "Terrible",
    1==1, "Unknown")
| stats count as streams,
    avg(packet_loss) as avg_loss,
    avg(jitter) as avg_jitter,
    perc95(packet_loss) as p95_loss,
    sum(eval(case(quality_rating="Bad" OR quality_rating="Terrible", 1, 0))) as poor_streams
    by participant_alias, conference_name, stream_type
| eval poor_pct=round(poor_streams*100/streams, 1)
| where poor_pct > 5
| sort -poor_pct
| table participant_alias, conference_name, stream_type, streams, avg_loss, avg_jitter, p95_loss, poor_pct
```
